key_insight: PINNs with exact boundary and initial constraints recover the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 accurately from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields without tuning boundary or initial-condition penalties.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a potential non-destructive route to characterizing shear-mode coupling in piezoelectric materials used in PMUTs and SAW devices.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers in network outputs to enforce clamped, grounded boundaries and a resting initial state.
Train on coupled electro-elastodynamic residuals and sparse wavefield observations, with nondimensional scaling to balance governing coefficients.
Infer e15 jointly with the wavefields, including tests using displacement-only observations.
evidence_signal: On finite-element data sampled along one subsurface line, the full formulation achieved 1.19% mean e15 error at 30 dB noise and 0.65–2.71% across a 40–0 dB noise sweep.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-only; performance on experimental measurements and imperfectly known boundary conditions remains untested.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
